articles.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
articles.summary: At least 21 people have died, five are missing and five others have been injured across Nepal after four days of torrential rain triggered floods and
articles.body: At least 21 people have died, five are missing and five others have been injured across Nepal after four days of torrential rain triggered floods and landslides in several parts of the country, authorities said on Sunday. The severe weather from September 24 to 27 also forced the evacuation of around 3,000 people and damaged or destroyed hundreds of homes.The latest warning came after the Narayani River in central Nepal crossed the danger level of nine metres on Sunday morning and entered settlements. Several highways leading to Chitwan, a key road junction connecting different parts of the country, also remained blocked by landslides.Authorities warned residents in low-lying areas to remain alert as the continuing rain increased the risk of further flooding and landslides.Landslides account for most deathsAccording to an update from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), landslides accounted for 14 of the deaths. Five people remain missing in landslide-related incidents.Floods have killed four people, while three others died following continuous heavy rainfall.A separate landslide in Nishikhola Village Council of Baglung district killed four people on Sunday morning, local authorities said.“In Nishikhola Village Council of Baglung District, four people have died after being buried in a landslide. The incident occurred this morning in Ward Number 3, Hardra,” Prem Bahadur Gharti Magar, the deputy chairperson of the village council, told ANI over the phone.The Kaligandaki River in Baglung has also swept away houses and bridges, cutting off road connectivity in parts of the district.Rivers blocked by landslidesNDRRMA earlier issued a high-alert advisory for people living along major river basins after landslides blocked or partly obstructed river flows.A landslide in Chame, the headquarters of Manang district, obstructed the flow of the Marsyangdi River. Another landslide in Nisi, Ward 3 of Thasang Rural Municipality in Mustang, partially blocked the Kali Gandaki River.The authority urged people living downstream to remain extremely cautious because of the risk of sudden water releases if the blockages give way.Landslides at several locations have also hampered search and rescue operations, while conditions continued to deteriorate because of the persistent rain.Thousands moved to safetyThe severe weather has directly affected 247 families across Nepal. NDRRMA said 260 homes were completely destroyed and another 80 suffered partial damage.Emergency teams have moved around 3,000 people from high-risk areas to safer locations. Armed Police Force personnel and local authorities have been involved in rescue and relief operations, including providing food and other essentials to displaced families.In the worst-hit mountain districts of Jajarkot, Myagdi and Sankhuwasabha, helicopters were used to evacuate people who were trapped.NDRRMA Spokesperson Shanti Basnet said district administration offices in all 77 districts, along with all three national security agencies, remained on high alert as authorities continued collecting data and carrying out recovery work.More than 100 locations record over 100 mm rainThe downpour was triggered by a low-pressure system originating in the Bay of Bengal, NDRRMA said.Its monitoring stations recorded more than 100 mm of rainfall at 106 locations during the four-day period.Dumkuali in Nawalparasi (Bardaghat Susta East) recorded the highest rainfall at 455.2 mm. Pokhara in Kaski received 407.2 mm, while Anbu Khaireni in Tanahun recorded 373.2 mm.As the storms intensified, NDRRMA's Central Monsoon Response Command Centre directed local authorities to stop vehicle movement on vulnerable road sections. Schools were also closed in affected districts.The agency sent more than 5,000 direct SMS alerts to field responders. The Flood Forecasting Division sent more than 814,000 early-warning messages to people living in downstream flood-risk areas.Tourists warned to avoid vulnerable areasThe bad weather has also raised concerns for thousands of foreign tourists and trekkers in Nepal.NDRRMA estimated that around 9,000 foreign tourists and trekkers were in the country during the period of heavy rain. In coordination with the Nepal Tourism Board and local trekking agencies, the authority issued safety advisories in English.Tourists in vulnerable terrain were urged to take shelter and suspend travel until conditions improved.Two bodies recovered after Himlung Himal avalancheNepal is also dealing with a separate disaster in the high-altitude Manang district.Two bodies were recovered after an avalanche at the base camp of Himlung Himal, according to NDRRMA and Nepal Police.The mountain region had experienced heavy snowfall for several days, forcing climbers to retreat from autumn expeditions. Others remained missing after Sunday's avalanche.At 7,126 metres, Himlung Himal is one of Nepal's high-altitude climbing destinations. Helicopter flights to the area require an additional permit, making rescue operations more difficult.Fresh disaster follows deadly Bhotekoshi floodsThe latest floods and landslides come about a month after the devastating Bhotekoshi floods, which have so far claimed more than 1,400 lives and left over 6,000 people missing, according to the information provided by authorities.The August 26 disaster began in riverside settlements in Rasuwa district before rapidly affecting neighbouring Nuwakot and Dhading.The floods caused extensive infrastructure damage. Eight operating hydropower projects with a combined capacity of 281 MW and four projects under construction with a combined capacity of 388 MW were damaged.Major sections of the Galchhi-Betrawati-Rasuwagadhi road and the Prithvi Highway were also destroyed or badly damaged. The disaster affected 48 suspension bridges and 31 motorable bridges.Nepal PM flags Himalayan climate risks at UNEarlier, Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah used his UN General Assembly address to highlight the growing risks facing the Himalayan region.He thanked India and China for their “prompt and generous assistance” following the August disaster.Shah said warming was destabilising the fragile Himalayan ecology by thawing permafrost and weakening mountain slopes. He said this was increasing the risks of ice-rock avalanches, floods, landslides and other cascading hazards.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Charles Baker started a two-person garage business in 1980 so his son could have a job; 46 years later, the nonprofit he built in Malvern has hired, trained and mentored more than 12,500 people
articles.summary: Charles P.
articles.body: Charles P. Baker III, who started a small business in his garage in 1980 to create a job for his son, went on to build an organisation that helped more than 12,500 people find work. Baker, who co-founded Baker Industries with his wife Louise, died on September 16 at the age of 101, The Philadelphia Inquirer reported.Baker Industries began with Baker, his wife and their son Justin. Justin lives with epilepsy and had struggled to find suitable employment. The family started a two-person mail-order packaging firm in their Strafford garage, with Justin becoming their first employee.The business later developed into Baker Industries, a workforce development nonprofit based in Malvern. Over nearly five decades, it hired, trained and mentored people who often faced difficulties finding jobs elsewhere, including people with physical and intellectual disabilities, substance use disorders, recent periods of incarceration and housing insecurity.The idea behind the organisation came from the Bakers' own experience. “We decided, if we’re going to start something like this, let’s go for the people who need it the most,” Baker told The Inquirer in 1998, “the ones who are least employable.”From a garage to a workforce programmeBaker Industries went on to contract light industrial and office work for hundreds of businesses. It operated facilities in Philadelphia, Malvern and other locations, while its employees were paid an hourly wage and given additional training.The organisation also encouraged workers to attend workshops, social events and support group meetings. Its motto was “providing a steppingstone to regular employment”, with many workers eventually moving to higher-paying jobs elsewhere.Baker described the approach as more than simply giving people jobs. “We have a philosophy of work as rehabilitation,” he told the Daily News in 1988. “The goal is to show these people they can do a whale of a lot more than they think they can do.”Baker remained involved with the organisation for decades. He served as its unpaid president until 2002 and then continued on its board of directors. Colleagues later remembered the work he and Louise had built around the idea that employment could play an important role in helping people move forward.“Charlie and Weezie Baker believed there is healing in work,” colleagues at Baker Industries said in a Facebook tribute on his 101st birthday in June. “Not just jobs. Work. Showing up. Being part of something. Contributing alongside others.”A different approach to hiringBaker Industries also took a different approach to people with criminal records or histories of drug use. Baker explained this in a Daily News interview in 1990.“We don’t screen out people who have a criminal record or who have used drugs because we know that’s a big part of why people become homeless.”He also called on other employers to focus on a person's present circumstances rather than only their past. “We need employers who will look at what these people are doing now instead of what they have done before,” he told the Daily News in 1998.The organisation and the Bakers received recognition for their community work. In 1991, Baker Industries was named an inspirational Point of Light by President George H.W. Bush. In 2004, Baker and his wife received the legacy award for “community generosity” from the Chester County Community Foundation.A foundation official told The Inquirer at the time that the couple “went above and beyond their own self-interest.”Nic Watson, president of Baker Industries, said Baker's example would continue to guide the organisation. “I was grateful to have their guidance,” Watson said, “and we will follow their example for years to come.”Baker's life beyond the organisationBaker's career before Baker Industries included running his family's chemical company. In the 1950s, he took control of C.P. Baker & Co., expanded the business and sold it in 1980.He had also served in the US Army after graduating from the US Military Academy in 1946. He spent more than seven years in the Army, was stationed in Europe and rose to the rank of captain.Away from work, Baker remained active for much of his life. He was a squash player, skier and sailor. He won the US national hardball singles squash championship six times in the 80-and-older division between 2006 and 2016. He skied into his 70s, sailed into his 80s and continued playing squash and tennis at the Merion Cricket Club until recently.Baker was born in Philadelphia on June 24, 1925. He grew up at the old Colonial Hotel at 11th and Spruce Streets in Washington Square West. His father, Charles Jr., was the hotel's manager. Baker's mother died when he was 11.He met Louise Wilhelm while water-skiing in Ocean City. They married in 1955 and had two sons, Charles IV and Justin, and a daughter, Sandra. Louise died in 2025.His family said he was a “relentlessly joyful spirit”. His daughter described him as a funny father who liked singing show tunes and writing corny poems on birthday cards. “He was a wonderful dad who loved his family,” she said.Baker died of congestive heart failure at HarborChase assisted living community in Wilmington. He is survived by his children, four grandchildren, five great-grandchildren and other relatives.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said on Sunday that Iran is prepared for a "doomsday" war with the United States, but stressed he was keeping diplomacy open so as not to "miss any chance for peace.""We stand firm in the face of any aggression against us, even if it comes to a doomsday war," Araghchi made the remarks during an interview with NBC News."If you ask us, there is no reason why we should go back to diplomacy, but I am still trying diplomacy because I think we shouldn't miss any chance for peace," Araghchi said. "We are ready to negotiate as much as we are ready to face any challenge."On Friday, Araghchi had proposed reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear negotiations with the US within seven days, provided the Trump administration agreed to Iran's conditions.However, US President Donald Trump rejected the proposal.According to the Wall Street Journal, Trump also expected to resume bombing Tehran once the US midterm elections concluded in November.In a separate NBC News interview, US ambassador to the United Nations, Michael Waltz, described Iran's latest offer as a "cynical attempt to put something on the table that they knew was unacceptable."Since the beginning of the war in late February, Iran has significantly disrupted traffic through the strait, curbing oil and gas exports from the Persian Gulf.US rejects captured underwater drone reportsMeanwhile, the US military has pushed back against claims by Iran's Revolutionary Guard that it had seized an advanced American underwater vehicle conducting surveillance in the Strait of Hormuz.US Centcom spokesman, captain Tim Hawkins, told Al Jazeera that the US maintains "positive control of all of our operational drone assets," brushing off the IRGC's claim as "clearly desperate."Earlier today, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced that it had seized a second advanced US unmanned underwater vehicle, the Remus 600, in the Strait of Hormuz, describing the operation as a "coordinated and complex" effort involving military intelligence and electronic warfare capabilities.You use AI every day. articles.title: An 8,000-acre South Carolina forest was bought for conservation after drawing developer interest; the state now plans to acquire 4,148 acres for a new Carvers Bay State Forest
articles.summary: Georgetown County School Board members voted to support state plans to buy two large pieces of land.
articles.body: Georgetown County School Board members voted to support state plans to buy two large pieces of land. The move could lead to a new 4,148-acre state forest in western Georgetown County and protect a former resort development site. The South Carolina Forestry Commission plans to buy the 4,148-acre property on Eaddy Road near Dunbar Landing. The land would become part of the planned Carvers Bay State Forest, the Coastal Observer reported. The larger conservation effort also includes plans for the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (DNR) to take over the 3,492-acre Arcadia East property on the Waccamaw Neck. Board Member Eileen Johnson supported the expansion during the meeting. She said continued residential growth in the area is leaving less space for nature. “We've got to preserve everything we can,” she said. Johnson added that the only thing protecting the south side of the county from development is the Francis Marion National Forest. “I'm all about stewardship of our land.”Creation of Carvers Bay State ForestThe 4,148-acre property planned for the state forest is part of a larger 8,000-acre tract. The Virginia-based Conservation Fund and the Malone Family Land Preservation Foundation bought the larger property last July for $34.2 million (£25.6 million). The rest of the land is next to the Black River. Once the South Carolina Forestry Commission completes the purchase, the property will become part of the state Department of Natural Resources wildlife management area program. This would allow the public to use the land for outdoor recreation. Under South Carolina law, state forests bring in money through local forestry work. The Forestry Commission gives 25 per cent of the gross revenue from those operations directly to the county. The money helps fund school district operations. “We can have public access,” Johnson said.Preservation of Arcadia EastThe school board also approved a letter supporting the purchase of the 3,492-acre Arcadia East property. Giving the coastal property to the state would stop a large commercial development that Georgetown County originally approved in 2002. The original development plan called for 2,451 homes, a 500-room resort hotel, and commercial and office space. A county study from 2002 estimated that a fully developed Arcadia East project could have produced as much as $153.8 million each year. Its residents would have become the largest taxpayers in the county. By moving the land into public conservation, local governments would give up those possible commercial revenues. They would also lose direct property tax payments from the undeveloped land. Last year, county and school district taxes on the Arcadia East property totaled about $5,200. DNR plans to complete the purchase with help from the Office of Resilience and two conservation nonprofits, the Open Space Institute and Ducks Unlimited. The nonprofits will hold the property title until state funding is finalized.Local backing for conservationThe Georgetown County Council also officially supported the land purchase during its meeting. The council joined the school board in backing the move toward conservation. Emily Purcell, director of conservation programs for Ducks Unlimited, said the organization was pleased to have local support for the purchase. “We're thrilled to have support from both the county and the school board,” Purcell told the Coastal Observer. “We're excited to hopefully work towards a great conservation outcome in Georgetown County.” The Arcadia East property adds to other protected land nearby. In 2007, a conservation easement was placed on 3,612 acres of Arcadia west of Highway 17. Ducks Unlimited currently holds and manages that land. Johnson also addressed concerns about losing future tax revenue from the resort property. She said protecting natural land was more important than collecting short-term tax revenue. “We've got plenty of land. I'm not worried about taxes right now,” Johnson said. Board Chairman Keith Moore and Superintendent Bethany Giles declined to comment on the vote.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 2,318 pujas apply on Sahaj portal, 270 new among them
articles.summary: Kolkata sees 270 new Durga Puja applications on Sahaj portal; 2,318 registered so far. Inspections begin Monday as totals may near last year’s record.
articles.body: Kolkata: It has been less than two weeks since the Sahaj portal – that allows one-point registration for Durga pujas in Kolkata along with Bengal – opened. According to Lalbazar, already 270 new Durga Puja permissions have been sought, with inspections over in most cases and a few already permitted to hold pujas.Almost all divisions have seen applications for new pujas, but Jadavpur and East division lead the way. Behala division and south Kolkata will also see a few “big” pujas like Allen Park in Park Street debut this year.Overall, 2,318 were registered till last Thursday on Sahaj portal so far, with another 10-odd days to go.Organisers and police claim these are mainly apartment pujas that are planning to leave their mark this year. “The added areas are witnessing several new complexes, some of whom had been planning to host a puja for the past three years. Several of these are exclusively being organized by women,” said Sandipan Banerjee of Forum For Durgotsab and the convener of Behala Natun Dal.Last year, a total of 2,936 organisers had applied for permission, the highest ever. Cops believe these numbers are likely to be challenged this year. Sources said that the city had hosted 2,757 Durga pujas in 2023 and 2,701 in 2022. The final numbers are expected to be firmed up a day prior to Mahalaya.The physical inspection of pandals by policemen is set to begin from Monday in Kolkata.The Jadavpur division last year saw as many as 28 new pujas, making the area’s number by far the highest number of community pujas in the city. There are at least a dozen new applications this year. “From 625 community pujas in 2021, the number of applications has gone up to 653 this year till now,” stated a police officer at Lalbazar. The Behala division hosted 561 pujas last year. The Eastern Suburban division hosted 327 pujas.The numbers are likely to rise even across Bengal. Over 43,000 pujas were held across Bengal, reaffirming the festival’s status as the state’s biggest cultural and religious celebration. Since Kolkata’s Durga Puja was inscribed on Unesco’s Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2021, Durga Puja has evolved into a global cultural attraction, drawing increasing numbers of domestic and international tourists.According to an estimate, overall, an estimated two crore people—including residents, domestic tourists and international visitors—are expected to join in pandal-hopping across Kolkata during the festival, making it one of the world’s largest public cultural gatherings.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Porter’s twin sons get NIT Rourkela key in 2nd attempt
articles.summary: Railway station porter’s twin sons crack JEE in second attempt, secure BTech admissions at NIT Rourkela, share hostel room; tuition fees waived.
articles.body: Rourkela: Rourkela railway station porter Sanjay Saw’s long-cherished dream has finally come true. His identical twin sons, Sachin and Sourav, both 20, have secured admission to the National Institute of Technology, Rourkela (NIT-R), and are now sharing the same hostel room.Sanjay, who lives with his wife and sons at Tingtang Gali in Gopabandhupali, near the railway station, said he had always been determined to provide his children with the best possible education despite his modest income.Sachin, who is 10 minutes older than Sourav, secured 96.7% in the ICSE Class X examination in 2023, while Sourav scored around 95%. Both completed Class XII from the same private English-medium school in 2025, with support from the school management.The brothers began preparing for JEE (Mains) while pursuing Plus Two, taking online coaching. After failing to secure a good rank in their first attempt, they took a year’s break and prepared for the entrance exam again.Sanjay, determined to support their preparation, rented a small room near their one-room house so that the brothers could study without distractions. He also approached a private coaching centre in Rourkela for a concession in coaching fees. Considering their academic record and the family’s financial circumstances, the institute charged them a minimal fee. The brothers underwent coaching for a year and worked hard to crack JEE in 2026.Sachin has secured admission to the BTech programme in electronics & instrumentation, while Sourav has joined the BTech course in industrial design. They were admitted to NIT-R in Aug and are now sharing the same hostel room.“In our first attempt, we could not secure a good rank and therefore, we had taken a drop. With dedicated private coaching, we cracked the entrance in 2026. The credit for our success goes to our parents, particularly our father, who worked very hard for our studies,” Sourav said.Echoing his brother, Sachin said, “The credit for our success goes to our parents. I am happy that both of us have got admission to NIT, Rourkela.”For Sanjay, seeing his sons at NIT-R is fulfilment of a dream he nurtured while working at the railway station. “While working at Rourkela railway station as a porter, I remember seeing students of NITR boarding trains and getting off them. I used to dream about when my sons would study at NITR. My dream has been fulfilled with God’s blessings,” he said.NIT-R registrar Rohan Dhiman assured that the institute would extend all possible support to the brothers during their studies.“Based on the income certificate of the father of these two students, their tuition fee was waived off for the first semester. articles.title: Rera seeks court intervention to complete stalled housing project
articles.summary: Goa Rera asks North Goa court to enforce its 2020 order for Hrija Construction to finish stalled housing project and hand over flats to buyers.
articles.body: Panaji: Goa Real Estate Regulatory Authority (Rera) has moved the North Goa principal district and sessions court to enforce its 2020 order directing Hrija Construction to complete an unfinished housing project and hand over flats to home buyers.The move follows representations submitted by aggrieved home buyers in July and Aug, more than six years after the authority ordered the developer to complete the project and give possession.On Sept 9, Rera secretary Dattaraj Gauns Desai re-initiated the execution proceedings, pointing out that the district court had considered only the portion of the authority’s order relating to possession, while overlooking its direction to complete the project.In Feb 2020, Goa Rera had imposed a Rs 15 lakh penalty on Hrija Construction for failing to register the ongoing project and deliver possession. It had directed the developer to complete the project and hand over the flats by April 30, 2020.After the developer failed to comply, Rera initiated criminal proceedings before the judicial magistrate first class (JMFC) for non-registration and forwarded the penalty recovery to the Revenue department. It also sent the order on completion and possession to the district court for execution.However, on June 23 this year, the ad hoc district court in Panaji closed the execution proceedings, observing that physical possession could not be handed over as the building was incomplete and did not have a final occupancy certificate (OC).Rera has now argued that obtaining an OC is an inherent part of completing the construction and that the execution proceedings should not have been closed merely because possession could not yet be handed over.The authority told the court that it has no power to review its order once it has been issued and urged the executing court to use its powers under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). articles.title: SHO, home guard staff held over corruption charges
articles.summary: Punjab Vigilance Bureau arrests Kot Ishe Khan SHO Sunita Bawa and home guard Guravtar Singh for alleged Rs 80,000 bribe; case filed under PC Act.
articles.body: Bathinda: The Punjab Vigilance Bureau has arrested Kot Ishe Khan police station SHO Inspector Sunita Bawa and Punjab Home Guard employee Guravtar Singh in a corruption case. As per sources, the home guard was arrested by the vigilance bureau late Saturday while accepting Rs 50,000 as illegal gratification. during interrogation, he claimed Bawa was also part of the plot. As the inspector called Guravtar to her office to hand over the money, and vigilance sleuths arrested her as well.Earlier, one Rajwinder Singh had approached the vigilance bureau, stating the police had demanded Rs 1 lakh from him by threatening to implicate him ina NDPS Act case. The matter was later settled for Rs 80,000. He recorded the conversation with the home guard on his mobile phone and handed it over to a vigilance inspector, who asked the complainant to go ahead to hand over the bribe money and prepared a plan to arrest the police officials.Vigilance Bureau Ferozepur Range SSP Jagatpreet Singh said that acting on a complaint, the VB has arrested Inspector Sunita Bawa and home guard Guravtar Singh in the presence of govt witnesses. articles.title: Customers flock banks in Chennai on Sunday
articles.summary: Chennai bank branches saw heavy Sunday rush ahead of a planned Sept 28–30 bank strike, later deferred; seniors led visits for cash, pensions and queries.
articles.body: Chennai: It was an unusual Sunday on First Avenue in Indira Nagar, Adyar, which is largely deserted during weekends. Customers thronged the road, which houses seven branches of public- and private-sector banks, including a small finance bank, within a 400m radius.The footfall was higher at public-sector banks in anticipation of banking operations being disrupted in view of the three-day strike called by bank unions between Sept 28 and 30, which has been deferred after meeting between banks’ association and unions.Banks were open on Sunday to offset the impact of the strike, as operations in public-sector banks and some old-generation private-sector banks were likely to be affected between Monday and Wednesday. However, branches of new-generation private-sector lenders were to remain open.There was a stark difference in footfall, with several bank branches in north Chennai being more crowded compared with those in the southern and central parts of the city.Senior citizens outnumbered other customers, while several visited for cash deposits and withdrawals, cheque clearances, and account-related queries. S Sundararajan, 77, who visited a Bank of India branch in Adyar for an account-related query, recalled how banks used to operate on Sundays for the convenience of residents. “I am a former bank employee and was part of the Sunday operations, though it was several years ago. Such branches used to function additionally on Sundays, mostly in residential locations,” he said.In north Chennai, the branches were thronged by a sizeable number of senior citizens to withdraw their pensions. Mohamed Asik, a visitor to an SBI branch in Washermenpet, said another reason for this was the convenience of Sunday operations. “Many have free time only on Sundays, and they used this opportunity to visit their respective branches,” he added.Banks were prepared for higher transaction volumes on Sunday. Indian Bank anticipated Sunday’s transaction volumes could be higher and prepared for this in advance. “Our branches and offices have been provided with adequate manpower, and our ATMs were replenished beforehand to ensure sufficient cash availability.
